raw_response:
66 mu is a decent stretch of land. I have been doing this for 6 years now so I have a feel for what works on my fields. Let me think through each crop.

**Wheat and Maize — the backbone**

About 50 mu of my land runs the wheat-maize rotation. That is the main thing. I sow wheat in mid-October after tilling the field. I use the Jimai variety — the seed shop near the township sells it and a neighbor two villages over got good results with it three years running. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at sowing, then chase with urea at jointing when the plants look like they need pushing. I water 3 to 4 times: once before sowing to wet the bed, once in winter to protect roots from the cold, once at jointing, and once at filling if it is dry. I spray herbicide early spring and a fungicide around heading — powdery mildew hits here some years.

After wheat harvest in June, I go straight into maize. I like to do no-tillage on that field — saves me time and the soil does not dry out as fast in the summer heat. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, almost everyone around here uses it. Maize needs heavy nitrogen — I put it in two shots, some at sowing with the machine and the rest top-dressed around the V6 stage. I only spray twice: once for weeds, once for corn borer if I see damage.

**Stevia — the cash crop**

I have about 10 mu in stevia. A company in the county contracts with farmers here to buy the dried leaf. The price is decent and it is more stable than grain. Stevia does not like standing water and my well irrigation helps me control that. I apply less nitrogen than on wheat — too much and the leaf quality goes down, the buyer complains. Potassium I give it a bit more. I harvest the leaves twice a season usually, cut and dry them. I spray 3 times: once for aphids, once for a fungal issue I had last year, once more as a precaution late season.

**Sweet potato — small plot, good return**

The remaining 6 mu I put into sweet potato. My family eats some and I sell the rest at the local market or to a starch processor nearby. Sweet potato loves potassium — I learned that from an input dealer who told me to put more potash and my yields went up noticeably the year after. I keep nitrogen low. I plough this field and make ridges — you have to for the tubers to form properly. I water maybe 2 or 3 times, less in wet years. Pests are not too bad, I spray twice.

**Budget thinking**

66 mu means I can invest in decent inputs and still make it work. But I am not wasteful — every bag of fertilizer costs real money. I would rather put 1 extra bag on the wheat than lose half the harvest to drought or nutrient shortage. Labor is the big constraint at harvest time, so I hire day workers for wheat and sweet potato.
